title: Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence
html:
1Definitions and Goals

Inmon Definition (Bill Inmon — "Father of the Data Warehouse")

"A subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, and non-volatile collection of data in support of management's decision-making process."

Property Meaning
Subject-Oriented Organized around key business subjects (customer, product, sales) not applications
Integrated Data from multiple sources reconciled into consistent format
Time-Variant Historical data; records data over time periods
Non-Volatile Data is not updated or deleted; only loaded and queried

Kimball Definition (Ralph Kimball)

"A copy of transaction data specifically structured for query and analysis."

Business Intelligence (BI)

Definition: Processes, technologies, and tools to transform raw data into meaningful and actionable information for business decision-making.

3 Goals:

  1. Support strategic, tactical, and operational decision-making
  2. Enable self-service reporting and analysis by business users
  3. Provide a single, consistent version of the truth across the enterprise

2Business Drivers

  • Reduce time to information for business decisions
  • Enable trend analysis and forecasting
  • Standardize reporting across the enterprise
  • Support regulatory reporting requirements
  • Enable performance monitoring against business goals (KPIs/scorecards)
  • Reduce costs of ad hoc reporting

3Seven Guiding Principles

  1. Focus on business requirements — technology serves business; requirements-first approach
  2. Start with a single subject area — iterative delivery; don't boil the ocean
  3. Think enterprise — design for enterprise reuse, even if delivering iteratively
  4. Promote data quality — DW/BI depends on high quality, trustworthy data
  5. Build for change — data models and architectures must accommodate evolution
  6. Maintain metadata — lineage, definitions, business rules documented
  7. Collaborate — DW/BI requires cooperation between IT and business stakeholders

4DW/BI Architecture Components

Operational Data Store (ODS)

  • Integration point for operational data from multiple systems
  • Contains current, near-real-time data (typically 30–90 days of history)
  • Used for operational reporting and as staging area for DW
  • Key: ODS is NOT the data warehouse; supports operational decisions

Data Warehouse

  • Central repository of integrated, historical data for strategic/analytical decisions
  • Inmon's CIF (Corporate Information Factory) — DW as central to enterprise architecture

Data Mart

  • Subset of the data warehouse for a specific department or business area
  • Can be dependent (sourced from DW) or independent (sourced directly from operational systems)

DW Bus Matrix

  • Kimball's tool for enterprise DW planning
  • Matrix showing which dimensions are shared across fact tables (subject areas)
  • Enables identification of Conformed Dimensions

Data Lake

  • Repository storing raw data in native format (schema on read)
  • Discussed in detail in Chapter 14

5Dimensional Modeling

Star Schema

  • Central fact table surrounded by dimension tables
  • Fact table: measurable, quantitative data (metrics)
  • Dimension tables: context for facts (who, what, when, where, how)

Snowflake Schema

  • Variation of star schema where dimension tables are normalized (split into sub-dimensions)
  • More complex; reduces redundancy; harder to query

Conformed Dimensions

  • Definition: Dimensions shared across multiple fact tables/data marts
  • Enable consistent reporting across subject areas
  • Example: Date dimension used by both Sales and Inventory fact tables
  • Key concept in Kimball's bus architecture

Fact Table Types

Type Description
Transaction Fact One row per transaction event
Periodic Snapshot One row per period (e.g., daily inventory balance)
Accumulating Snapshot One row per lifecycle event with multiple date stamps

6OLAP (Online Analytical Processing)

Purpose: Multi-dimensional analysis of data (vs. OLTP for transactions).

MDX (Multidimensional eXpression): Query language for multidimensional/OLAP databases.

Three OLAP Types

Type Storage Key Fact
ROLAP (Relational OLAP) Relational database Queries relational tables via MDX translation
MOLAP (Multidimensional OLAP) Proprietary multidimensional cubes Fastest query performance; pre-aggregated
HOLAP (Hybrid OLAP) Combination of relational + multidimensional Balance of storage efficiency and performance

7Change Data Capture (CDC) Techniques

Purpose: Identify and capture only changed data to reduce load on data warehouse ETL.

Technique Description
Audit Columns Source tables have Created_Date and Updated_Date columns; ETL reads changed rows
Database Triggers Source DB fires trigger on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; captures changes to staging table
Full Table Comparison Compare full source snapshot to previous; identify differences; resource-intensive
Database Transaction/Redo Logs Read database transaction log; most efficient; non-invasive
Message Queues Source systems publish change events to message queue; ETL subscribes

8ETL / ELT Process

ETL Phases (Standard)

  1. Extract — Read data from source systems
  2. Transform — Apply business rules, cleanse, convert, aggregate
  3. Load — Write to target (staging area, data warehouse, data mart)

Staging Area

  • Temporary storage between source and target
  • Allows transformation, reconciliation, and error handling before final load

9BI Delivery Components

Reporting and Analytics Types

Type Description
Standard/Operational Reports Recurring reports for daily/weekly operations
Ad Hoc Reports User-defined queries on demand
Dashboards Visual display of KPIs; real-time or near-real-time
Scorecards Performance measurement against strategic objectives
OLAP Analysis Slice, dice, drill-down, roll-up on multidimensional data
Predictive Analytics Statistical models to forecast future outcomes

Self-Service BI

  • Business users create their own reports without IT involvement
  • Requires well-designed data models and governed Metadata

10Key Terminology

Term Definition
Grain The level of detail captured in a fact table (e.g., one row per daily sales transaction)
Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Dimension attribute that changes over time; Type 1=overwrite, Type 2=new row, Type 3=history column
Surrogate Key Artificial key assigned in DW to uniquely identify dimension members; independent of source system keys
Degenerate Dimension Dimension stored directly in fact table (no separate dimension table); e.g., order number
Factless Fact Table Fact table with no measures; records events (e.g., student attendance)
OLTP Online Transaction Processing — operational systems; row-oriented; high-frequency transactions
OLAP Online Analytical Processing — analytical/DW systems; column-oriented; complex queries

11Data Governance in DW/BI

Key Governance Areas:

  • Data lineage — track data from source through transformation to target
  • Metadata management — business definitions of all DW objects
  • Data quality — validate data before loading; monitor ongoing quality
  • Access control — control who can access sensitive data in reports
  • Change management — manage source system changes affecting DW

DW Metrics:

  • Report freshness (latency between source and DW)
  • Data quality error rates (records rejected in ETL)
  • Query performance (response time)
  • User adoption (number of active users, reports run)
  • Availability (DW uptime)

12Practice Q&A

Q1: What are the 4 properties of a data warehouse per Inmon's definition? A: Subject-Oriented, Integrated, Time-Variant, Non-Volatile.

Q2: What is Kimball's definition of a data warehouse? A: "A copy of transaction data specifically structured for query and analysis."

Q3: What is an ODS and how long does it typically retain data? A: Operational Data Store — integration point for near-real-time operational data; typically retains 30–90 days of history.

Q4: What is a conformed dimension? A: A dimension shared across multiple fact tables or data marts, enabling consistent reporting across subject areas (key concept in Kimball's bus architecture).

Q5: What is the DW Bus Matrix? A: Kimball's tool for enterprise DW planning; a matrix showing which dimensions are shared across fact tables/subject areas; identifies conformed dimensions.

Q6: What are the 3 OLAP types? A: ROLAP (Relational OLAP — relational DB), MOLAP (Multidimensional OLAP — proprietary cubes, fastest), HOLAP (Hybrid — combination).

Q7: What is MDX? A: Multidimensional eXpression — query language for multidimensional/OLAP databases.

Q8: What are the 5 CDC techniques? A: Audit Columns, Database Triggers, Full Table Comparison, Database Transaction/Redo Logs, Message Queues.

Q9: What is a star schema? A: A dimensional model with a central fact table surrounded by dimension tables; optimized for query performance.

Q10: What is the difference between star schema and snowflake schema? A: Star schema has denormalized dimensions; snowflake normalizes dimensions into sub-dimensions (more complex to query, less redundancy).

Q11: What are the 3 fact table types? A: Transaction Fact (one row per event), Periodic Snapshot (one row per period), Accumulating Snapshot (one row per lifecycle).

Q12: What is a Surrogate Key? A: An artificial key assigned in the DW to uniquely identify dimension members, independent of source system keys.

Q13: What is a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD)? A: A dimension attribute that changes over time; Type 1=overwrite old value, Type 2=add new row with history, Type 3=add history column.

Q14: What is the difference between OLTP and OLAP? A: OLTP = Online Transaction Processing (operational, row-oriented, high-frequency transactions); OLAP = Online Analytical Processing (analytical, column-oriented, complex queries).

Q15: Who is known as the "Father of the Data Warehouse"? A: Bill Inmon.

13Quick Reference

Concept Key Fact
Inmon Definition Subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile
Kimball Definition Copy of transaction data structured for query/analysis
"Father of DW" Bill Inmon
ODS Near-real-time; 30–90 days history; operational decisions
DW Historical, integrated, subject-oriented; strategic decisions
Data Mart Subset of DW for specific department/area
DW Bus Matrix Kimball tool; maps dimensions to fact tables
Conformed Dimensions Shared across fact tables; enable consistent reporting
Star Schema Fact + denormalized dimensions; best query performance
Snowflake Normalized dimensions; more complex
ROLAP Relational storage; MDX translation
MOLAP Proprietary cubes; fastest; pre-aggregated
HOLAP Hybrid; balance of performance and storage
MDX Query language for multidimensional OLAP
SCD Type 1 Overwrite old value
SCD Type 2 New row with history
SCD Type 3 Add history column
CDC Techniques Audit Columns, Triggers, Full Compare, Redo Logs, Message Queues
Grain Level of detail in fact table
Surrogate Key Artificial DW key independent of source
OLTP Row-oriented; operational transactions
OLAP Column-oriented; analytical queries
7 Guiding Principles Business req, single subject, think enterprise, quality, change, Metadata, collaborate
